source.title: An Internet for the KV Cache: Rethinking Classical Infrastructure Boundaries in the LLM Inference Age
source.summary: LLM inference has become a global-scale, heterogeneous workload spanning agents, retrieval, tool-use, code execution and multi-modal reasoning. These workloads naturally enable context reuse from overlapping inputs, creating a major opportunity to store and reuse the contexts' KV Caches instead of recomputing them. However, model-side advances that shrink the KV Cache and system-side advances that reduce compute, storage, and transfer costs are evolve independently within legacy cloud boundaries. We argue that future inference infrastructure should allow decoupling of compute and KV Cache storage across cloud and datacenters. The network becomes an active distribution channel; bandwidth, latency and pricing directly determines how the KV Cache should be managed. We propose a vision for an Internet for the KV Cache, with KV Cache management working as a content-distribution system. In this view, KV Cache storage and recompute decisions are driven by model, infrastructure, and application metrics, to enable adaptive, content-driven decisions for minimizing latency and cost.

previous_facts.title: An Internet for the KV Cache: Rethinking Classical Infrastructure Boundaries in the LLM Inference Age
previous_facts.event_hint: Vision paper proposing global-scale KV Cache content distribution system
previous_facts.problem: Model-side KV Cache optimizations and system-side transfer/storage optimizations evolve independently within legacy cloud boundaries, preventing optimal placement of compute and KV Cache storage across clouds and datacenters
previous_facts.mechanism: Proposes 'Internet for the KV Cache' vision where KV Cache management works as content-distribution system with global control plane (directory service, placement planner, prefetch scheduler) enabling store-anywhere-use-everything with bandwidth-aware movement and reuse-horizon-based tiering (hot/warm/cold)

evidence.claim: Transferring 1 GB KV Cache over fully utilized 10-Gbps link is ~19x faster and ~5.2x cheaper than AWS 8xB200 GPU cluster compute
evidence.condition: 1 GB KV Cache transfer over fully utilized 10-Gbps link

evidence.claim: Storage-compute locality is core restriction in cloud pricing due to egress costs dominating bulk data movement
evidence.condition: Wide-area cloud movement is slow and egress prices dominate cost

evidence.claim: KV Cache reuse horizons span seconds to hours in agentic workflows, enabling temporal slack for storage-compute tradeoffs
evidence.condition: Agentic workflows with multi-step reasoning, tool calls, code execution

evidence.claim: Placement governed by jointly considering reuse rates, deadlines, bandwidth, transfer and recomputation costs
evidence.condition: Model metrics (prefill FLOPs, KV size), infrastructure metrics (GPU/storage cost, bandwidth), application metrics (reuse frequency, turns)
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 1, Abstract and PDF Page 2, Introduction section

evidence.claim: Paper positions as 'call for arms' rather than implemented system
evidence.condition: Vision paper without concrete implementation or evaluation

previous_facts.evaluation_context: Vision paper without empirical evaluation. Quantitative examples drawn from public cloud pricing documents and prior work. Proposes three-tier storage model (hot near GPU, warm intermediate, cold distant) driven by reuse horizons. References existing systems: SkyPilot, SkyServe for inter-cloud compute; Mooncake for disaggregated KV Cache; various cache compression/eviction techniques.
previous_facts.limitations: Vision paper without implemented system or end-to-end evaluation. Transfer cost comparison assumes fully utilized 10-Gbps link; real-world WAN conditions with congestion, variable latency not modeled. No quantitative assessment of control plane overhead, consistency mechanisms, or failure handling. Does not address multi-tenant security or cache poisoning risks.
previous_facts.project_relevance: Directly addresses TPN project questions on whether network can感知 KV Cache placement and whether network-side optimization adds value beyond GPU memory scheduling. Vision proposes network as active distribution channel where bandwidth/latency/pricing directly determine KV Cache management. However, lacks concrete TTFT/TPOT measurements or comparison to state-aware network scheduling. No implementation to validate whether proposed global control plane actually improves token throughput or P95 latency versus current cloud-local approaches.

evidence_gaps.question: What are the quantitative TTFT, TPOT, or P95 latency improvements from implementing the proposed Internet for KV Cache versus current cloud-local approaches?
What are the control plane overheads for KV Cache directory lookup, placement planning, and prefetch scheduling in real-time inference workloads?
How does the proposed system handle consistency, eviction, and multi-tenant isolation across regions and clouds?
